snippet.title: Commodore 64 Longplay (Telarium) Dragonworld 1984
snippet.description:
Dragonworld is an illustrated fantasy text adventure for the Commodore 64, developed by Byron Preiss Video Productions and published by Telarium in 1984. It is based on the 1979 fantasy novel Dragonworld by Byron Preiss and Michael Reaves, continuing the story of the novel as an interactive adventure.

The player takes the role of Amsel of Fandora, who receives a warning through the mystical Dragonpearl that the Last Dragon has been kidnapped and is being held in the land of Simbala. Amsel sets out to find his friend Hawkwind, ruler of Simbala, and together they begin the search for the captive dragon.

The adventure takes the player through three large geographical regions and more than 150 rooms, filled with puzzles, characters, dangerous creatures and hidden objects. Amsel must manage money and supplies, examine his surroundings, collect useful items and communicate with inhabitants by asking questions about specific subjects. Hawkwind accompanies him for much of the journey and can provide advice or perform certain tasks himself.

The Dragonpearl is particularly useful. It can be invoked a limited number of times to remove Amsel from danger and transport him to a safer location. The game therefore combines conventional adventure-game problem solving with a few special fantasy mechanics that fit naturally into its story.

The C64 version uses high-resolution illustrations together with a text parser, with the player entering commands through the keyboard. It is a single-player adventure, and the parser supports more sophisticated commands than the simple verb-noun systems found in many early adventures.

Some versions of Dragonworld also contain three arcade-style mini-games: Bogs and Bats, Maze of Madness and Dragonstones. These can be encountered during the main adventure, although different editions of the game vary in whether the arcade sequences are included. The C64 release containing them was particularly substantial, with surviving documentation describing a multi-disk release.

The game received strong contemporary attention, with Computer & Video Games awarding the Telarium release 9/10. Its combination of detailed graphics, atmospheric fantasy writing and an ambitious parser made it one of Telarium's more substantial early literary adventures.

For a C64 collection, Dragonworld is an important example of Telarium's literary-adventure approach, combining an original fantasy novel, illustrated interactive fiction and optional arcade sequences into a much larger package than a conventional early text adventure.

Notable people

Byron Preiss — Author of the original Dragonworld novel, co-writer of the game's story and head of Byron Preiss Video Productions.

Michael Reaves — Co-author of the original Dragonworld novel and contributor to the game's story.

J. Brynne Stephens — Writer responsible for additional text material for the game.

Lee Jacknow — Technical design and direction.

Michael P. Meyer — Senior systems programmer; also credited as the C64 coder in C64-specific sources.

John Pierard — Principal illustrator, with additional illustrations by Walter Martishius.

Walter Martishius — Additional illustrations for the game.

Robert Strong — Contributed to the arcade-game designs and other aspects of the production.

Howard Boles — Musician credited on the Commodore 64 version.

Telarium Corporation — Publisher of the C64 release; the company was originally founded as Trillium before changing its name in 1984.

------------------------

It is a shame the loading times from most Telarium game are very slow. A .crt conversion would really help here.
